artists.biography:
The B-52s are an American rock band, formed in Athens, Georgia in 1976. The original line-up consisted of Fred Schneider (vocals, cowbell), Kate Pierson (vocals, keyboards), Cindy Wilson (vocals, tambourine, bongos), Ricky Wilson (guitar), and Keith Strickland (drums). Following Ricky Wilson's death in 1985 Strickland switched to guitar. Then they added Tracy Wormworth (bass), Sterling Campbell (drums) and Paul Gordon (keyboards).

Rooted in New Wave and 1960s rock and roll, the group later covered many genres ranging from post-punk to pop rock. The "guy vs. gals" vocals of Schneider, Pierson, and Wilson, sometimes used in call and response style ("Strobe Light," "Private Idaho", and "Good Stuff"), are a trademark. Presenting themselves as a positive, enthusiastic, slightly oddball party band, the B-52s tell tall tales, glorify wild youth, and celebrate wild romance. The band name had long been "The B-52's", until 2008 when they dropped the apostrophe and are now "The B-52s"

perplexity.description:
Released on June 27, 1989, by Reprise Records, Cosmic Thing is the fifth studio album by The B-52's and marks a pivotal moment in the band's career. Musically, the album blends rock and pop with danceable rhythms, catchy hooks, and the band's signature quirky style, while incorporating a more polished, mainstream production compared to their earlier underground new wave sound. Produced by Don Was and Nile Rodgers, Cosmic Thing features the hit singles "Love Shack" and "Roam," both of which became defining tracks of the era and helped reestablish the band's commercial presence.

Cosmic Thing was the group's first album following the death of guitarist Ricky Wilson and their return after a three-year hiatus. It represented a shift toward a more accessible sound, broadening their appeal beyond their new wave roots. The album was a major commercial success, becoming The B-52's most popular release and earning critical acclaim for its energy and resilience. It solidified their place in pop culture and remains a standout in their discography for its blend of fun, dance-rock, and heartfelt tribute to their late bandmate.
